holidays.name: Back to the Future Day
holidays.description: Fans of the DeLorean, flux capacitors and 1.21 gigawatts gather to celebrate the day Marty McFly and Doc Brown zoom into the future. Expect movie marathons, hoverboard jokes and a lot of people squinting at the sky for flying cars.
holidays.origin: Back to the Future Part II (1989) sends its heroes to October 21, 2015. When that real date arrived, fans turned the movie's fictional date into an annual celebration of the trilogy.
holidays.funFact: The movie got a few things right, including video calls, smart glasses and tablet-style screens. Even so, we're still waiting on the self-lacing sneakers and the flying cars.

holidays.name: Count Your Buttons Day
holidays.description: A cheerfully odd observance that asks you to count every button within reach. That means shirts, coats, remote controls, jars full of spares and the mystery button on your jeans.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a quirky fixture on October calendars.
holidays.funFact: Buttons began as decorations thousands of years ago. They only became common as fasteners in Europe in the 13th century, when buttonholes were invented.

holidays.name: National Reptile Awareness Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate snakes, lizards, turtles, crocodiles and all the other scaly, cold-blooded creatures. Visit a reptile exhibit, learn about conservation, or just give your neighborhood gecko a respectful nod.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Reptile fans use it to encourage understanding and protection of these misunderstood animals.
holidays.funFact: Many reptiles can go weeks or even months between meals. Some large snakes can go much longer after one big meal.
